2610.12436.title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
2610.12436.paper_summary: AI agents can now conduct real-world cyberattacks, scale up capabilities with the number of agents, and collectively pursue misaligned goals to obtain rewards. Together, these factors raise the risk of a population explosion of misaligned agents: agents could compromise computers and secretly deploy additional agents, creating a self-reinforcing cycle where larger populations develop greater collective cyber capability and expand further. This raises a fundamental question: What determines whether a population of misaligned agents remains contained or takes off into this self-reinforcing cycle? This population-level problem is ecological safety: unlike individual-agent or multi-agent safety with a fixed population, it concerns the dynamics of the population itself. Here, we develop an ecological theory of AI-agent populations based on a population growth equation in which fitness (growth rate) depends on cybersecurity capability. We show that, without collaboration, the population takes off only when individual-agent capability exceeds a critical threshold. With collaboration, however, collective cybersecurity capability increases with population size. This creates a critical population threshold: below it, the population declines; above it, the population takes off, even though individual-agent capability has not changed. In ecology, this phenomenon is known as the strong Allee effect. Because red teaming a small group of agents cannot guarantee ecological safety in larger populations, our theory calls for ecological red teaming and population pacing: gradually deploying larger agent populations in controlled environments, while measuring how cyber capability scales with population size, and estimating the critical population size for takeoff. Capability gains may lower this threshold, requiring re-estimation for each new model generation.
2610.12436.paper_summary_zh: AI代理現在可以進行現實世界的網路攻擊，隨著代理數量的增加而擴大能力，並共同追求不一致的目標以獲得獎勵。<lb/>這些因素共同提高了不一致代理人口爆炸的風險：代理可能會入侵電腦並秘密部署額外的代理，形成一個自我增強的循環，其中更大的群體發展出更強的集體網路能力並進一步擴展。<lb/>這提出了一個根本性問題：什麼決定了一個不一致代理的群體是保持受控還是進入這個自我增強的循環？<lb/>這個群體層面的問題是生態安全：與擁有固定人口的單一代理或多代理安全不同，它關心的是群體本身的動態。<lb/>在這裡，我們基於一個人口增長方程開發了一個AI代理群體的生態理論，其中適應度（增長率）取決於網路安全能力。<lb/>我們顯示，沒有合作時，只有當單一代理的能力超過臨界閾值時，群體才會起飛。<lb/>然而，隨著合作的進行，集體網路安全能力隨著人口規模的增長而增加。<lb/>這創造了一個臨界人口閾值：低於這個閾值，人口會下降；高於這個閾值，人口會起飛，即使單一代理的能力並未改變。<lb/>在生態學中，這種現象被稱為強阿利效應。<lb/>因為對小型代理群體進行紅隊測試無法保證在更大群體中的生態安全，我們的理論呼籲進行生態紅隊測試和人口節奏控制：在受控環境中逐步部署更大的代理群體，同時測量網路能力如何隨著人口規模增長，並估算起飛的臨界人口規模。<lb/>能力的增長可能會降低這個閾值，要求對每一個新模型世代進行重新估算。
2610.12436.author: Erin Crawley et.al.
